ex-E304-1.title: Comparing stability of different nucleus
ex-E304-1.question:
The mass of a carbon-12 (C-12) nucleus,

C-12 nucleus

11.996 710 u

proton

1.007 276 u

neutron

1.008 665 u

a proton and a neutron in atomic mass unit (u) are given in the table.

(a) A C-12 nucleus has 6 protons and 6 neutrons. Calculate its binding energy and binding energy per nucleon in MeV.

(b) The mass defect of a uranium-234 (U-234) nucleus is 1.909 380 u. Explain whether the nucleus of C-12 or U-234 is more stable.
ex-E304-1.answer:
(a) Δm = 6 × 1.007 276 + 6 × 1.008 665 − 11.996 710 = 0.098 936 u

Binding energy = 0.098 936 × 931 = 92.1 MeV

Binding energy per nucleon = 92.112 = 7.68 MeV

(b) Binding energy per nucleon of U-234 nucleus = Δm × 931A

= 1.909 380 × 931234

= 7.60 MeV

C-12 nucleus is more stable because its binding energy per nucleon is larger.

ex-E304-2.title: Energy released in a fission reaction
ex-E304-2.question:
The following equation shows one possibility when a nucleus of uranium-235 absorbs a neutron and splits into lighter nuclei.

01n + 92235U → 56144Ba + 3689Kr + 301n

The table below shows the binding energy per nucleon of the particles.

Particle

Binding energy per nucleon / MeV

92235U

7.590 937

56144Ba

8.265 550

3689Kr

8.616 942

(a) Find the energy released in the reaction in (i) MeV and (ii) J.

(b) State the change in the total mass of particles in the reaction.
ex-E304-2.answer:
(a) (i) Binding energy of 92235U = 7.590 937 × 235 = 1783.87 MeV

Binding energy of 56144Ba = 8.265 550 × 144 = 1190.24 MeV

Binding energy of 3689Kr = 8.616 942 × 89 = 766.91 MeV

Energy released = 1190.24 + 766.91 – 1783.87 = 173 MeV

(ii) Energy released = 173 × 106 × 1.60 × 10−19 = 2.77 × 10−11 J

(b) Decreases

ex-E304-3.title: Determine type of reaction from binding energy curve
ex-E304-3.question:
X and Y are two different nuclides. Their positions on the binding energy curve are shown on the right.

(a) Estimate the binding energy of Y from the curve.

(b) Which nuclide is more likely to undergo fusion? Explain.
ex-E304-3.answer:
(a) Binding energy = 8 × 200 = 1600 MeV

(b) X is more likely to undergo fusion. This is because if X undergoes fusion, the nuclide formed will have higher binding energy per nucleon and is more stable. On the other hand, if Y undergoes fusion, the nuclide formed will have lower binding energy per nucleon and is less stable.

ex-E304-4.title: Power of Lamma Winds
ex-E304-4.question:
In Lamma Winds, the blades of the wind turbine are 25 m long. A wind blows with a constant speed of 5.56 m s−1. Take the efficiency of the turbine as 35%, and the air density as 1.225 kg m−3.

(a) Find the maximum power generated by the wind turbine in kW.

(b) If the wind speed increases by 50%, what will the maximum power become? Assume the efficiency of the turbine remains the same.
ex-E304-4.answer:
(a) Maximum power = 12ηρAv3

= 12 × 35% × 1.225 × (π × 252) × 5.563

= 72.3 kW

(b) As P ∝ v3, if v increases by 50%,

maximum power = 72.3 × (1 + 50%)3 = 244 kW

ex-E304-5.title: Efficiency of a hydroelectric power station
ex-E304-5.question:
In a hydroelectric power station, the water level of the upper reservoir is 60 m above that of the lower one. Water flows from the upper to the lower reservoir at a rate of 5 m3 s−1 and turns a turbine below the water level of the lower reservoir. The turbine is connected to a generator.

Given: density of water = 1000 kg m−3, g = 9.81 m s−2

(a) Find the rate of loss of the potential energy of the water in MW.

(b) The output power of the station is 2.5 MW. Find its efficiency.
ex-E304-5.answer:
(a) Rate of loss of PE of water

= mght = (mt)gh = (5 × 1000) × 9.81 × 60 = 2.94 MW

(b) Efficiency = power outputpower input × 100% = 2.52.94 × 100% = 85.0%

ex-E304-6.title: Power received by a surface
ex-E304-6.question:
A satellite is on the outer surface of the Earth’s atmosphere. It has a plate of area 0.64 m2. Sunlight falls on the plate and the solar constant is 1366 W m–2. Estimate the total power received by the plate if the sunlight is incident

(a) normally,

(b) at 60° (Fig a).
ex-E304-6.answer:
(a) Total power received = solar constant × area

= 1366 × 0.64

= 874 W

(b) Total power received = (solar constant × cos θ) × area

= (1366 × cos 60°) × 0.64

= 437 W
ex-E304-6.location: Book E3  |  Chapter E304  |  Source PDF p. 23

ex-E304-7.title: Solar water heater
ex-E304-7.question: A solar water heater has a flat collector of area 4 m2. It is illuminated normally by sunlight for 30 minutes to heat water. The solar constant is 1366 W m–2. The atmosphere absorbs 25% of the power of solar radiation. If the efficiency of the heater is 45%, estimate the solar energy absorbed by the water.
ex-E304-7.answer:
Power of solar radiation per unit area on the Earth’s surface

= 1366 × (1 − 25%) = 1025 W m–2

Energy collected by the collector = 1025 × 4 × (30 × 60) = 7.38 × 106 J

Energy absorbed by the water = 7.38 × 106 × 45% = 3.32 × 106 J
